title: Emergent Andreev Reflection from a Lattice Duality Defect
authors: Atsushi Ueda, Tokiro Numasawa, Boris De Vos, Masataka Watanabe
abstract: Andreev reflection converts an incoming fermion into an outgoing hole and is usually tied to a superconducting interface. We show that an analogous charge-conjugating boundary condition emerges from a purely lattice duality defect. Starting from a Majorana representation of the transverse-field Ising chain, we construct a folded lattice model in which a boundary Majorana impurity implements a one-site translation of a staggered Majorana chain. In the continuum, this translation becomes a chiral fermion-parity defect: it flips the sign of the only left-moving Majorana mode while leaving the right-moving mode unchanged. When the two Majorana modes are recombined into a complex fermion in the folded geometry, this sign flip becomes the Andreev-like boundary condition. Our lattice formulation gives a microscopic interpretation of the Emery--Kivelson boundary of the two-channel Kondo problem and of Maldacena--Ludwig monopole scattering, while identifying the boundary as the interface between a Kitaev-chain SPT phase and a gapless chain. The same Majorana translation defect also provides a lattice realization of an axial $U(1)_A$-symmetric charge-flip boundary.
summary: The paper reveals that Andreev reflection, typically associated with superconducting interfaces, can emerge microscopically in a purely lattice system by introducing a duality defect into the transverse-field Ising chain. This mechanism is mathematically equivalent to a specific one-site translation of Majorana fermions, providing a unified theoretical framework for understanding boundary physics across different quantum impurity models.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the universal mechanism behind Andreev reflection (a charge-conjugating boundary condition) when it appears in seemingly unrelated quantum impurity problems, such as those related to the two-channel Kondo effect.
main_result: Andreev reflection is shown to emerge naturally from a purely lattice duality defect—specifically, it corresponds to a one-site translation of Majorana operators within the folded transverse-field Ising chain model.
method: The authors use theoretical mapping techniques, transforming the Ising Hamiltonian into a Majorana representation and analyzing scattering dynamics by 'folding' the system at an impurity site.
model_or_system: The primary model is based on the transverse-field Ising chain, which is analyzed via its Majorana fermion formulation. The defect introduces an effective boundary condition analogous to those found in the Emery–Kivelson (EK) model or at interfaces between Kitaev-chain SPT phases and gapless chains.
key_observables: Scattering dynamics of wavepackets, charge fluctuation ($\delta n(x)$), comparison between free vs. EK boundary conditions, and conservation laws for axial $U(1)_A$ symmetry.
important_parameters: The system is analyzed in the continuum limit and at the interface between a Kitaev-chain SPT phase and gapless chains; the two-channel Kondo problem serves as a key physical realization.
main_assumptions: The identification of Andreev reflection with a one-site translation defect is termed 'emergent' because it is not an exact microscopic equality on the lattice, but rather a low-energy statement.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the mapping from the Ising chain to the folded geometry, comparing scattering results for free vs. EK boundaries, and showing the physical realization of Andreev reflection via Majorana impurity defects acting as chiral fermion-parity defects.

why_interesting: This work provides a deep microscopic understanding of topological boundary phenomena, linking concepts from condensed matter (Kitaev chains, SPT phases) to fundamental quantum impurity physics (Kondo effect) via lattice symmetries and defects.

Solid and dashed lines denote couplings of alternating strength. (b) The same model after sliding the decoupled Majorana fermion βobs. βobs forms a pair with the fifth Majorana (which we call the active Majorana, shaded in grey) for spanning the Hilbert space. (c) The folded representation of the impurity Ising chain.

FIG. 2. Scattering dynamics for the free boundary condition in (a,c) and the Emery–Kivelson (EK) boundary condition in (b,d), at g = 1 in (a,b) and g = 3 in (c,d). The wave packet is created by applying a fermion creation operator to the ground state which propagates toward the boundary at x = 1, where it is reflected. For the free boundary condition in (a,c), the charge of the excitation is preserved upon reflection. For the EK boundary condition in (b,d), the charge is flipped.

FIG. 3. Andreev reflection in the lattice EK model. (a) Before unfolding, a wavepacket of the complex fermion approach- ing the boundary decomposes into a pair of chiral Majorana fermions hopping in the same direction. (b) After unfolding, the pair of chiral Majorana fermions move in opposite direc- tions towards the impurity. (c) The boundary Majorana im- purity implements a one-site translation, producing a minus sign only for the left-moving mode. (d,e) Continuum coun- terpart of the same process. The Majorana impurity acts as a chiral fermion-parity defect.
